deities: Kandoliya Devta (folk guardian deity, identified with Shiva)

history.period: 12th century CE (attributed; based on visitor reviews, not scholarly sources - verify)
history.summary: Hilltop temple to Kandoliya Devta, the guardian deity of Pauri town, on Kandolia Hill overlooking Pauri in Pauri Garhwal district. DATE NOTE: a 12th-century Katyuri origin is claimed in visitor reviews only; no scholarly source found - treat as unverified (flag). Local legend says a Kumaoni bride of the Dungriyal Negi community brought the deity in a small basket (kandi), hence the name Kandoliya. The temple is surrounded by cedar and oak forest with Himalayan views; nearby are Kandoliya Park, a sports complex and the Ransi stadium. The annual Jai Kandolia Mahotsav (week-long, with folk rituals, sports and music) and an annual bhandara are major events. CSV state correction: the state column holds town names; the real state is Uttarakhand (town Pauri is correct). Opening hours not documented in any source consulted (flagged).

name: Kandoliya Devta Temple
town_description: Pauri is the headquarters town of Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, on the northern slopes of the Kandoliya Hills at about 1,765-1,814 m. Known for Himalayan views (Bandarpoonch, Kedarnath group) and Garhwali culture.

travel.road: Well connected by motorable roads from Dehradun, Rishikesh, Haridwar and Kotdwar; a short climb of about 200 steps (or side road) leads to the hilltop temple
